messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the L3 split RFC — proposing a lightweight \"auth-edge\" service between the Dashboard UI and the query plane to centralize RBAC + define a clear caching boundary. Want feedback on latency tradeoffs and fallback semantics.

james: +1 on separating auth concerns, but worried about an extra network hop increasing p99. Can we keep auth inline for the hot read path and only route slow/complex checks to auth-edge? @maya

anita: If we take auth-edge, it must be cache-friendly. Ideas: per-token TTLs, negative cache for missing perms, and a small decision table for short-circuiting checks. Also add a bulk endpoint so UI can check multiple panel perms in one round trip.

ryan: Batching at the auth-edge could help throughput but adds latency. Suggest an async pre-warm: UI hits an \"auth-assert\" on navigation to prepopulate checks for the most likely panels. That keeps interaction latency low.

lina: Ops note: more services = more things to run. Need graceful fallback: if auth-edge is down, dashboard should have a deterministic fallback — either direct checks against the query-plane (slower) or a conservative deny. We should decide fail-open vs fail-closed by route sensitivity.

samir: PoC perf numbers (staging): auth-edge median +1ms, p99 ~6–8ms with LRU cache(50k). If we add batching window 10ms, that was +2ms median but p99 jumped to ~20ms. I'll attach graphs to the RFC.

maya: For the interface boundary, propose auth-edge exposes two endpoints: /check and /check-bulk (for batched resource checks). Minimal request shape:

```json
{"user_id":"...","resource":["dash:panel:123","dash:view:456"],"action":"read"}
```

Response should be per-resource allow/deny plus optional reason code for auditing.

james: Keep the schema minimal. Also require passthrough of x-request-id for tracing and an audit header so downstream logs can correlate.

anita: We need token versioning/invalidation. Add a \"vtag\" header to requests so cache entries can be invalidated on permission changes. Also include an audit hook (async) to write denial events.

ryan: Cache key must be conservative: include user role fingerprint, resource version, and panel template version. Otherwise permission flips or template changes will be stale and cause correctness issues.

lina: Operational playbook question: should the circuit-breaker fail closed (deny) when auth-edge is unreachable? That protects data but will cause outages for many dashboards. I think fail-open for read-only/public dashboards with strict alerts; fail-closed for admin/write actions.

samir: Compromise: make fail behavior configurable per-route/perm-sensitivity. Default: fail-open for low-sensitivity reads, fail-closed for anything tagged \"modify\" or \"admin\". We'll log and increment a dedicated metric so on-call can triage.

maya: Migration plan outline: Phase 1 = staging rollout, Phase 2 = 10% tenant opt-in with canary routes, Phase 3 = default routing. Telemetry required: auth-edge hit/miss, cache evictions, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and denied-counts by reason.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-1 to staging at 2468001300 — status: running.

james: One more perf note — shard the cache by tenant id to reduce noisy neighbor evictions. Also consider LFU eviction to keep frequent checks hot.

anita: Security: use HMAC-signed requests between UI edge and auth-edge, with key rotation. No need for KMS-heavy signing for now, but we should spec rotation cadence.

ryan: I'll draft a follow-up RFC that includes definitive endpoints, headers, cache semantics, rollout plan, and the ops playbook. @maya can you own opening it and include Samir's PoC numbers?

maya: Yup — I'll open the RFC tonight and own the ops playbook. I'll add the performance graphs and the per-route fail-open/closed table. Thanks all :thumbsup:
